howItWorks: Choose your audio, quality and format, then press Start recording and pick a screen, window or browser tab in the prompt your browser shows.
Record as long as you like — use Pause and Resume if you need a break, then press Stop & save (or use your browser’s Stop sharing button).
Preview the video in the page and press Download recording to save it to your device.

faq.a: No. The recording is created by your browser and kept on your device. It is never sent to a server, and nothing is stored or logged.

faq.q: Can I record sound from my computer?
faq.a: Browser tab audio works in Chrome and Edge when you tick the Share audio box in the picker. Whole-system audio is only offered on Windows. On other setups, record tab audio or use your microphone.

faq.q: Which browsers and devices are supported?
faq.a: Desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari can record the screen. Most phone and tablet browsers do not allow screen recording from a web page, so use your device’s built-in recorder there.

faq.q: Is there a time limit or watermark?
faq.a: There is no watermark and no fixed time limit. The recording is held in memory until you stop, so very long high-quality sessions can use a lot of memory — choose the Small file quality for long recordings.

faq.q: Why is my file a WebM, and can I get an MP4?
faq.a: WebM is the format most browsers can record. If your browser supports MP4 recording (recent Chrome, Edge and Safari), choose MP4 for wider compatibility with editors and phones.
